And again in Baghdad, two blind Arab men entered upon another blind man at night in one of the mosques and killed him,
because they thought they would find coins with him.
And when morning dawned,
they were afraid and went out to flee to Mosul.
And a certain executioner {or inspector}, who was going about another matter, met them
and said as if in jest,
"These blind men killed that blind man,
for no one kills a blind man except a blind man."
Then one of them, when he heard the word of the executioner, sat on the ground and said,
"By God, it was not I,
but this one killed him!"
And that other one said,
"No,
rather you killed him!"
And they were both seized and brought to the governor.
And they confessed
that one of them held him,
and the other strangled him with a blanket {or sheet}.
And both of them were executed.
And in the year 602
[602] of the Arabs,
a tribe of Kurds in the mountains of Media who are called Tirahis descended from the mountains,
and they caused great devastation in those regions.
And the Persian forces assembled and encountered them,
and many of them were killed.
For these people had not entered the religion of the Muslims,
but remained in their former paganism and Magianism.
And when a Muslim fell into their hands,
they would put him to death with bitter torments.
For when a daughter was born to any one of them,
he would stand at the door of his house and call out,
"Who will betroth this one?" And if someone accepted,
he would let her live;
and if not,
he would kill [her].
And for this reason women are scarce among them,
and for this reason there is only one wife for all the sons of a single household.
And when one of them is with her,
he leaves his shoes as a sign at the door,
so that when another sees it,
he will not go in to her
until his companion comes out,
and then he may enter.
And the child who is born,
the eldest among them is called his father.
And in the year 603
[603] of the Arabs, the Georgians again came to the region of Akhlat,
and they took captives, burned, killed, and departed.
And Ghiyath al-Din Kaykhusraw also took Antalya (Attaleia,
Satalia), a city on the seashore, on the third of the eighth month.
